name: Bharat H Parajia
current_role: Co-promoter / significant shareholder of the IIFL group (IIFL Finance, IIFL Securities, 5paisa); Singapore-based
profile: Bharat Himatlal Parajia is a Singapore-based investor and part of the promoter group of India's IIFL (India Infoline) financial-services group, previously listed as a managing director of IIFL Asia. Third-party filings data show stakes of ~4.4% in IIFL Finance, ~3.6% in IIFL Securities and ~2% in 5paisa Capital (2023).
interesting_fact: Holds stakes across three listed IIFL-family companies (IIFL Finance, IIFL Securities and online broker 5paisa Capital).
notes: Low public profile; no personal site or social accounts found. Best route is likely via IIFL group corporate communications. Alive status not confirmed by a recent public source.

name: Yugandhar Reddy
current_role: Associated with Medha Servo Drives, Hyderabad (per Hurun India 2017-2019); current role unverified
profile: Listed on Hurun India 2017-2019 (~US$132m) for Medha Servo Drives, a Hyderabad-based maker of railway traction/propulsion electronics founded in 1984 that also makes solar inverters. Public searches did not surface a profile tying this name to the company; registry listings show other Reddy family members (e.g. Kasyap Reddy Yadavelli) as directors.
interesting_fact: Medha Servo Drives runs a joint venture with Austria's Traktionssysteme Austria (TSA) that has produced over 10,000 traction motors in Hyderabad.
notes: Very private family-owned company; identity could not be confirmed online. Searches mostly return an unrelated Hyderabad oncologist with a similar name. Medha's solar-inverter line may be relevant to an energy podcast.

name: Mark A Goldsmith
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, Revolution Medicines (Nasdaq: RVMD)
profile: Mark A. Goldsmith, MD, PhD (Princeton; UCSF) has led Redwood City-based Revolution Medicines since 2014, building it around RAS(ON) inhibitors for RAS-addicted cancers. Its lead drug daraxonrasib showed a major overall-survival benefit in the Phase 3 RASolute 302 trial in previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer and was reported FDA-approved (as RASONQUE) in Aug 2026.
interesting_fact: In April 2026 Revolution reported daraxonrasib met all primary and key secondary endpoints, including overall survival, in a pivotal Phase 3 trial in metastatic pancreatic cancer, one of the hardest-to-treat cancers.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech management he was an academic HIV researcher: a UCSF School of Medicine faculty member who ran a research lab at the Gladstone Institute of Virology and Immunology; he later founded and led Cogentus Pharmaceuticals (2006-09) and ran Constellation Pharmaceuticals.
notes: Biotech, not energy; podcast angle would be entrepreneurship/company-building. Deep-cut source (The Org) is marked unverified; career history is corroborated by MarketScreener bio pages. Aug 2026 FDA approval taken from company release summarized in search results.

name: Arthur G. Sulzberger
current_role: Chairman, The New York Times Company, and Publisher of The New York Times
profile: A.G. Sulzberger (b. 1980), fifth-generation member of the Ochs-Sulzberger family, became publisher of The New York Times in 2018 and company chairman in 2021. A former reporter (Providence Journal, The Oregonian, NYT Kansas City bureau), he led the 2014 Innovation Report and has steered the Times' shift to a subscriber-first digital business.
interesting_fact: He was lead author of the Times' 97-page 2014 Innovation Report, a blunt internal assessment of how the paper was losing ground to digital rivals that leaked to BuzzFeed and became a widely read industry document.
deep_cut_fact: The 2017 film 'Kodachrome' (Ed Harris, Jason Sudeikis, Elizabeth Olsen) was inspired by his 2010 NYT article on Parsons, Kansas, the last place in the world to develop Kodachrome film. As a Providence Journal intern he exposed a Narragansett Lions Club's men-only membership; it began admitting women months later.
notes: booking@nytimes.com is listed by NYTCo as the 'Press: Media Requests' address (for booking Times people on outside media), the natural route for a podcast invitation. Media-business rather than energy angle; he speaks publicly on press freedom and AI/copyright.

name: Vikas Jain
current_role: Co-founder, World of Play (PLAY wearables/audio brand); co-founder of Micromax Informatics
profile: Vikas Jain is one of the four co-founders (with Rahul Sharma, Rajesh Agarwal and Sumeet Kumar) of Micromax, the Gurgaon company that grew from an IT venture into one of India's largest budget phone brands. He later co-founded World of Play, which sells affordable smart wearables and audio products aimed at young Indian consumers.
interesting_fact: In a DNA interview he said the Micromax founders 'never thought we would sell 1.8 million handsets a month', a volume the company reached at its peak.
deep_cut_fact: He was the fourth partner to join Micromax Informatics in its pre-phone era as a computer-training/IT venture; co-founder Rajesh Agarwal recalled: 'Later on, Vikas too joined us, chipping in his share of capital.'
notes: Consumer electronics, not energy. Micromax's fortunes declined after ~2016; avoid that topic. Hurun appearances 2015-2018 only. No published press email found for World of Play.

name: John Kent Walker
current_role: President, Global Affairs and Chief Legal Officer, Google & Alphabet
profile: Kent Walker (Harvard BA 1983, Stanford JD) has been Google's top lawyer since 2006 and President of Global Affairs since 2021, overseeing legal, policy, government affairs and trust & safety. He oversaw creation of Google's 2018 AI Principles and is a leading voice on AI regulation, digital sovereignty and the energy/infrastructure needs of AI.
interesting_fact: In a March 2026 post he argued AI developers should compete on demonstrable privacy techniques, calling it 'not just privacy by default, or even privacy by design - it's privacy by innovation.'
deep_cut_fact: Before Google he was a federal prosecutor (Assistant U.S. Attorney for five years), then a lawyer at AirTouch Communications and deputy general counsel at Netscape (1997-2001) during the browser wars, followed by Liberate Technologies and eBay.
notes: Strong fit for data-center/energy policy topics (Google's AI infrastructure and power advocacy). Best route is Google's press team; he publishes regularly on blog.google.

name: Preetha Reddy
current_role: Executive Vice Chairperson, Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd
profile: Dr. Preetha Reddy, eldest daughter of Apollo founder Dr. Prathap C. Reddy, has spent nearly four decades building Apollo Hospitals, India's largest private hospital group, joining management around 1989 and later serving as managing director before becoming executive vice chairperson. She shares the family's stake in the listed company with her sisters.
interesting_fact: She brought proton therapy to India: the Apollo Proton Cancer Centre in Chennai (2019) was the first such facility in South East Asia and the Middle East and has treated over a thousand patients.
deep_cut_fact: She championed India's first Joint Commission International (JCI) hospital accreditation, won by Apollo Indraprastha in Delhi in 2006, and credits her father's lesson that 'any aspect will be a problem, only if you decide to see it as one.'
notes: Healthcare, not energy. Has appeared on ET's 'Corner Office Conversation' podcast with sister Suneeta Reddy (https://omny.fm/shows/corner-office-conversation/corner-office-conversation-with-apollo-s-dr-preetha-and-suneeta-reddy). Apollo's website blocked automated access, so no corporate press/IR email could be verified; route via Apollo corporate communications.

name: Arie Kotler
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, ARKO Corp. (Nasdaq: ARKO), parent of GPM Investments
profile: Israeli-born Arie Kotler, in the U.S. since 1997, founded GPM Investments in 2003 by buying the Fas Mart and Shore Stop c-store chains, regained control in 2011 and built Richmond, Virginia-based ARKO into one of the largest U.S. convenience-store and fuel operators through serial acquisitions. ARKO went public on Nasdaq via a 2020 SPAC merger with Haymaker II.
interesting_fact: GPM had about 200 stores in seven states when Kotler took over as CEO in 2011; by 2022, after 21 acquisitions and some 5,000 stores vetted, it ran roughly 1,400 stores in 35 states. 'We're an acquisition company. We have it in our blood.'
deep_cut_fact: Before ARKO's Nasdaq listing he chaired and ran Arko Holdings Ltd., a Tel Aviv Stock Exchange-listed company that controlled GPM, so the U.S. c-store roll-up was originally financed through the Israeli capital market.
notes: Fuel retail/energy-adjacent (c-stores plus fuel wholesale), a good energy-podcast fit. Named to Virginia Business power lists 2025 and 2026. IR email is published on the ARKO homepage.

name: Srinivasan Sivaram
current_role: President and CEO, QuantumScape Corp (NYSE: QS)
profile: Dr. Siva Sivaram, a semiconductor-memory veteran (Intel, Matrix Semiconductor, SanDisk; Western Digital President of Technology and Strategy 2019-23), became CEO of solid-state battery developer QuantumScape in 2024. He has steered it toward a capital-light licensing model, including a 2024 deal with Volkswagen's PowerCo targeting up to 40 GWh/yr of production.
interesting_fact: QuantumScape's solid-state cell passed its first endurance test as independently confirmed by VW's battery unit PowerCo, and the company has also partnered with grid-storage firm Fluence, extending its batteries beyond EVs.
deep_cut_fact: Long before batteries he was a solar entrepreneur: in 2008 he founded Twin Creek Technologies, a U.S. maker of solar manufacturing equipment, and ran it as CEO for five years. He holds a mechanical-engineering BS from NIT Trichy (Distinguished Alumnus) and a materials-science PhD from RPI.
notes: Excellent fit for an energy/storage podcast; he has done many media interviews (Bloomberg, CNBC, 'E For Electric'). Commonly known as Siva Sivaram. info@ is a general company inbox.

name: Kathryn A Mikells
current_role: Former SVP and CFO, Exxon Mobil (Aug 2021 - retired effective 1 Feb 2026)
profile: Kathryn Mikells was ExxonMobil's Senior Vice President and CFO from August 2021 until her retirement on 1 February 2026, succeeded by Neil Hansen. She joined Exxon from Diageo plc, where she was CFO and a board director (2015-2021); earlier CFO roles reportedly included Xerox, Nalco and United Airlines.
interesting_fact: She was recruited to ExxonMobil's CFO job from consumer-goods group Diageo (Johnnie Walker, Guinness), where she had been CFO and a main-board director for nearly six years.
notes: Retired from Exxon Feb 2026 for personal reasons (per Exxon 8-K, Dec 2025: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408825000122/xom-20251208.htm); outreach should be gentle and should not raise the reason. Not currently in an executive role; earlier CFO roles (Xerox, Nalco, United) not verified in this pass.

name: Timothy John Fitzgerald
current_role: CEO, The Middleby Corporation (Nasdaq: MIDD) until 1 April 2027; director, Alliance Laundry Holdings
profile: Tim FitzGerald has spent nearly three decades at Elgin, Illinois-based Middleby (commercial kitchen and food equipment), serving as CFO before becoming CEO in 2019. In 2026 he led its biggest transformation: selling 51% of the residential kitchen business to 26North and spinning off food processing as Midera, leaving a pure-play commercial foodservice company. He hands the CEO role to Steve Spittle on 1 April 2027.
interesting_fact: On 9 Nov 2026 Middleby announced his succession, with the chairman crediting him with building 'the industry's broadest portfolio of leading commercial foodservice brands'; FitzGerald said 'with the portfolio transformation complete the timing is right'.
notes: Timely: CEO transition just announced (Nov 2026); he may be more available for long-form conversation after April 2027. Company HQ switchboard (847) 741-3300 is published on the release. No press/IR email found on the release page.

name: Earl A Steinert Jr
current_role: Director, Great Southern Bancorp (Nasdaq: GSBC), Springfield, Missouri; owner, EAS Investment Enterprises Inc.
profile: Earl A. Steinert Jr. (89 per the 2026 proxy) is a Springfield, Missouri accountant and real-estate investor who practised as a CPA from 1962 until retiring in 2006. He owns EAS Investment Enterprises, which owns and operates hotels in Springfield, previously ran apartment owner Mid-American Real Estate Partners, and has been a Great Southern Bancorp director since 2004.
interesting_fact: He practised public accounting for 44 years (1962-2006) while building a hotel and apartment portfolio in Springfield, Missouri on the side.
notes: Low-profile regional businessman; listed in 2026 proxy (filed Mar 2026), so alive as of then. Hospitality/real-estate and community banking; weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Only formal route is via Great Southern Bancorp corporate secretary.

name: Matthew Joseph Tobolski
current_role: CEO and Director, AAON, Inc. (Nasdaq: AAON), since May 2025
profile: Matt Tobolski, a structural engineer (UMass Dartmouth BS; UC San Diego MS/PhD), co-founded BASX Solutions in 2013 and became part of HVAC maker AAON when it acquired BASX in 2021, rising to President/COO and then CEO in May 2025. BASX-branded data-center cooling now drives AAON's growth: 2025 sales rose 20% to US$1.44bn and backlog more than doubled to US$1.83bn.
interesting_fact: AAON's backlog jumped 110.9% in 2025 to $1.83bn on demand for its data-center cooling products, prompting a large expansion including a Memphis, Tennessee facility bought in Dec 2024.
deep_cut_fact: Before HVAC he was an earthquake engineer: he ran Tobolski Watkins Engineering, a structural and seismic engineering firm, from 2008 to 2017, and is a licensed civil and structural engineer in California, Oregon and Washington.
notes: Excellent fit for a data-center/energy podcast (liquid and air cooling for AI data centers). AAON also runs its own 'Inside AAON' video/podcast series. AAON IR and officer pages block automated access, so no press/IR email verified.

name: Matthew Paul Duffy
current_role: President (since Apr 2025) and Chief Risk Officer, Neptune Insurance Holdings (Neptune Flood; NYSE: NP)
profile: Matt Duffy joined St. Petersburg, Florida-based Neptune Flood, a technology-driven private flood-insurance provider, in 2021 as head of risk management and internal audit, becoming Chief Risk Officer in 2022 and President in 2025. Neptune listed publicly in 2025. He previously led enterprise technology at Bank OZK and enterprise risk at C1 Bank.
interesting_fact: At Bank OZK he was EVP and Director of Enterprise Technology Solutions, overseeing digital process automation, software development and data visualization, before moving into insurtech.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an unusual four-way stack of credentials: Financial Risk Manager (FRM), Chartered Property Casualty Underwriter (CPCU), Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) and Project Management Professional (PMP), on top of an economics BA from Eckerd College.
notes: Insurtech/climate-risk angle (flood risk modelling) rather than energy. SEC Form 144 filings in Nov 2026 show planned share sales; not relevant for outreach.

name: Brian P Cassidy
current_role: President, Partner and Head of Media, Crestview Partners (New York private equity)
profile: Brian Cassidy joined private-equity firm Crestview Partners in 2004 and is now its president, an investment-committee member and head of its media strategy. He sits on the boards of Camping World (since 2011) and Pursuit Attractions & Hospitality as a Crestview designee, plus private companies including Saber Interactive, Framestore/Company 3, Hornblower and The Gersh Agency; he was on WOW!'s board until its Dec 2025 acquisition.
interesting_fact: His board portfolio spans an unusual mix: video-game maker Saber Interactive, visual-effects house Framestore/Company 3, talent agency Gersh, cruise operator Hornblower, and Australian rail-tourism company Journey Beyond.
deep_cut_fact: Early in his career at Boston Ventures he stepped in as acting CFO of portfolio company ec-Content, after starting as an investment-banking analyst at Alex. Brown & Sons.

public_contacts.value: Jeffrey Taufield, Kekst & Company (media inquiries for Crestview), (212) 521-4815

notes: Insider holdings reported under his name are largely Crestview fund positions (he has assigned director equity awards to Crestview Advisors), so personal wealth may be overstated. Congruex (fiber/telecom infrastructure) and Digicomm holdings could give a data-infrastructure angle.

name: Shuji Nakamura
current_role: Founder, Blue Laser Fusion, Inc.; Professor of Materials and ECE, UC Santa Barbara
profile: Shuji Nakamura (b. 1954, Ikata, Ehime) invented the first commercial high-brightness blue gallium-nitride LED at Nichia in 1993, sharing the 2014 Nobel Prize in Physics. A UCSB professor since 1999 and U.S. citizen since 2005, he co-founded lighting firm Soraa and in 2022 Blue Laser Fusion, which is developing high-peak-power pulsed lasers for fusion energy and directed-energy defense and went public via a US$34m alternative public offering in Oct 2026.
interesting_fact: Blue Laser Fusion's GigaPulse laser aims to deliver gigawatts of peak power, over 100,000 times conventional continuous-beam lasers, targeting both inertial-confinement fusion power and drone/missile defense.
deep_cut_fact: When Nichia's leadership halted the gallium-nitride project, he kept working on it on his own and succeeded in 1993; Tokushima University later awarded him a PhD by publication (1994), based on his published research rather than a conventional dissertation.
notes: Top-tier fit for an energy podcast (fusion). His UCSB faculty email is published by the university. Avoid the old Nichia patent-compensation dispute. Also holds the 2006 Millennium Technology Prize and 2021 Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering.

name: Brian Chambers
current_role: Board Chair, President and CEO, Owens Corning (NYSE: OC)
profile: Brian Chambers has spent 20+ years at Toledo, Ohio-based building-materials maker Owens Corning (insulation, roofing, doors), running its Composites and Roofing businesses and serving as President/COO before becoming CEO in 2019 and Board Chair in 2020. He earlier held commercial and operational roles at Saint-Gobain, Honeywell and BOC Gases, and sits on the board of Lincoln Electric.
interesting_fact: Beyond Owens Corning he sits on the board of the National Association of Manufacturers and the policy advisory board of Harvard's Joint Center for Housing Studies, giving him a voice on U.S. housing and manufacturing policy.
deep_cut_fact: Before Owens Corning he worked in industrial gases at BOC Gases, then Honeywell and Saint-Gobain; at Owens Corning he ran the Composites (glass fiber) business before Roofing, a path from industrial materials to the C-suite.
notes: Building materials and energy efficiency (insulation) angle. Owens Corning newsroom blocked automated access; no press email verified.
